title: Prognosticon spirituale. Oder Geistlicher Calender unnd Practica
shelf_note: A 1613 German Fraktur devotional 'spiritual prognostication' that sets Scripture against astrological almanacs. It matches its catalogue record. No tradition or collection is given to test it against.
structure_note: The counts disagree with each other: structure.pages_translated is 0, but pages_translated_field is 57 (of 60), and this page has a translation. One of the two instruments is wrong. with_printed_number is 0, which fits this leaf: it carries a running head and a catchword but no printed page number. There are no backsteps, repeats or duplicate records.

pages.layout: single column of Fraktur with Antiqua loan-words, running head over a rule, scripture references in the left (outer) margin, catchword at the foot; the book's fore-edge is visible on the left

ocr_errors.problem: initial v silently normalised to u, though elsewhere the OCR keeps v ('vnd', 'vmb')
the same v→u normalisation, inconsistent with the rest of the page

other.note: The running head 'Geistlich Prognosticon.' is promoted to a top-level heading, '# Spiritual Prognostication', in the reader's English.
The meta 'continues from previous page: "Yes, many say, the calendars often speak of many..."' quotes the previous leaf. I cannot check it from this page.

items.quote: a proverbial expression: they miss the mark by a wide margin

missing.english: Just ask the first world, which
missing.why: 'the first world' means the world before the Flood. A general reader will not know this, and the argument that follows depends on it.

book_verdict: A faithful page. The OCR is near-exact, with only two silent v→u normalisations, and the translation is accurate. All five notes and glosses are correct and drawn from the words. The only blemishes are cosmetic: the running head shown as a heading, and the book's translated-page counts contradicting each other.
